title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Where do the steps of a command handler that are the same for every command live?
description: ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05 puts code that is the same for every declaration in the runtime library, and the query runtime has an HTTP helper for it (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17), but the command runtime has none: the binding of the verified tenant and principal, the idempotency key, the decode, the call of Run, the map of ErrDenied, a declared refusal, ErrConflict and ErrCommitUnknown to 403, the declared status, 409 conflict and 500 internal, the outcome audit row and the problem body. The command generator writes these once per service in commands/handlers/serve.go, and only the spec of each command varies. Options: (A) add a command.Serve and command.ServeRPC helper to the runtime with a library contract of ST-SUP-RP10, and the generator emits only the spec; (B) keep the emitted helper, and record an exception to ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05. Recommendation: A, because the steps are the same for every command and their tests then live once in the runtime. The same holds for the helpers of the contract package that never change: the type Refusal, mustEntity, NewID, ValidUUID, clonePointer and equalPointer, which the generator writes once per service.

title: At which consistency does the decision of a command's permission run?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC06-T01 expects the decision for reserve on order:o1 at the consistency at_least t5, the authz_token of the row. ST-SUP-RC32-OC06 says the decision runs at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, and ST-SUP-RP10-LC31, after the review of PR #178, makes Run decide with the same consistency whether or not the row exists, so it reads the row FOR SHARE but does not give its token to the decision: the decision is at the floor, fresh while the floor is zero. Options: (A) change the Then of ST-SUP-RC32-OC06-T01 to the consistency of the floor; (B) change ST-SUP-RP10-LC31 to decide at the row token when the row exists. Recommendation: A, because one consistency for a missing and a present row keeps the deny of a missing row the same in time and calls. The test proves the floor consistency now.

title: What must the completion log of a failed command hold?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC09-T01 expects the completion log of ST-SUP-RP03-LC12 to hold only the code internal, and then the code reservation.short_stock. The completion log of the telemetry runtime holds the span fields only, the method, the route and the status, and no error code or text (ST-SUP-RP03-LC06), so it can hold no code. Options: (A) change the Then to expect that the completion log holds neither the email nor the SQL text, which its fields give; (B) add the fixed error code to the completion log in the telemetry runtime. Recommendation: A, because the status already tells the outcome and a smaller log leaks less. The test proves the response and the audit row now.

title: How many audit rows does a committed command leave?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 says the handler writes one audit row per command, and ST-SUP-RC32-OC07-T01 expects one command audit row with the outcome ok for a committed command. The command runtime writes one row for each write of the fill, with the command name as the action (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06), and no row for the command itself, so reserve-and-charge leaves two ok rows, one for its Reservation and one for its Charge. Options: (A) change ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 and its test to one ok row per write, with the command as the action; (B) add one ok row for the command itself to the runtime. Recommendation: A, because each row then holds the before and after of one resource. The test proves the rows of the writes now.

title: What does a command declare of its effect destinations and effect names?
description: The generated CommandSpec gives each effect destination of a command to the runtime as command.Destination with MustLand and Idempotent, but ST-DECL-EN18 declares only the destination and the effect name, and the destinations setting of a component gives only a name, so the generator sets MustLand and Idempotent to true for every destination. The runtime's CommandSpec also takes no effect names, so a fill can stage an effect name that the command does not declare; the generator refuses only a missing, malformed or repeated effect name in the declaration. Options: (A) the destinations setting declares must_land and idempotent for each destination, the generator reads them, and CommandSpec takes the declared effect names, which Stage then holds the fill to; (B) keep must land and idempotent for every command destination, and add only the effect names to CommandSpec; (C) keep both as they are. Recommendation: A, because the outbox worker registers each destination with these two properties and a staged effect should be one that the declaration names.
